processList.title: Processes
processList.empty: No processes with audio sessions found
processList.emptyHint: Play sound in the target app, then refresh
processList.multiSelectHint: Click to select; Ctrl+click to pick several and route them together

deviceVolume.valueLabel: Volume of {{device}}, relative to the loudest device, in percent
deviceVolume.hint: Attenuates this device relative to the loudest one in its group. Drag sideways, or scroll / press arrows for {{step}}% a time (hold Shift for ten); click to type an exact value

deviceDelay.hint: Drag sideways, or scroll / press arrows for {{step}} a time (hold Shift for ten); click to type an exact value
deviceDelay.syncOff: Latency sync is off, so these values are not applied; enable it in the settings

settings.title: Settings
settings.autoRememberDesc: Remember each process's device routing and restore it automatically
settings.delaySyncDesc: Compensate faster devices to align with a slower (Bluetooth) one
settings.resetEndpointsDesc: Gives every program its own output device back, except the ones a route is using right now. A program an earlier version left fixed to a device ignores the system default until this is done.
settings.closeToTrayDesc: The close button hides the window while every route keeps running, and the tray icon brings the window back. Turned off, closing quits the app and stops the routes with it.
settings.autostartDesc: Launches into the tray with no window at sign-in, so remembered routes are ready before you open anything.
settings.delayNote: Every device's delay is set against the app's audio; a route is applied in delay order, so the device the OS plays directly is the earliest one and becomes the alignment reference. On the main screen, drag the number under a device node, or scroll it.
settings.delayRangeDesc: Delays can be set within this ± range
settings.delayStepDesc: How much each − / + click changes; an exact value can also be typed
settings.aboutDesc: Per-app audio routing for Windows — Rust talking to Windows Core Audio directly, no third-party executables.

startup.upgradeTitle: An earlier version ran on this PC
startup.upgradeBody: It may have left some programs fixed to one output device: they no longer follow the device you switch to in Windows, and a reboot does not bring them back. If you hit one, clear it with the button below; if not, there is nothing to do.
startup.upgradeBodyVersion: The last version to run on this PC was {{version}}, and it may have left some programs fixed to one output device: they no longer follow the device you switch to in Windows, and a reboot does not bring them back. If you hit one, clear it with the button below; if not, there is nothing to do.
startup.resetHint: This clears every program that is running now, including a device you set by hand in the volume mixer. A program that is not running keeps its device until it starts.
startup.resetDone: Cleared the fixed output device of {{n}} program(s).
startup.resetRemaining: {{processes}} could not be cleared — let it play a sound and try again.
startup.firstRunBody: Pick a program that is playing on the left, click a device on the right, then press the button in the middle and the sound moves there. Pick several devices to play on all of them at once. If a program ever stops following the devices you switch to in Windows, the reset in Settings releases it.
